# 6. History, implementation and evidence

The Evidence and references tab in the central specification collects code anchors and scoped previous results. Immutable event and wave-origin history is distinct from a Node's bounded active references and does not authorize remote history reads. Cancellation must follow the selected branch causally without deleting past records, unrelated paths or spatial topology. Exact bounded lookup, stopping, conflicting-notice and future-packet handling still require closure. A return undoes a share of an event on the board; it does not rewrite the recorded history, and no event is moved. (Under the Beam Law, 2026-09-19, section 5.4: there is no return and no cancellation; the click is the only one-way border, and what a run records is in [the engine](ENGINE.md).)

Git documents and source code describe particular software interfaces and experimental profiles; each result applies only to its identified source revision and tested scope. Existing generic-contact or capture samplers do not by themselves satisfy the Detector-only rule of section 3.19. Older shared-clock profiles and an incomplete six-output-clock candidate do not establish the complete adopted engine contract. Candidate annexes support implementation review but cannot silently replace adopted definitions. Bell results recorded with the former shared resource (section 3.18, deleted) are historical and are not evidence for the current model, and PASS/RETURN values carried on returning rays do not by themselves establish entanglement or spacelike Bell correlations. This documentation review adds no simulator execution or new passing result.

# 7. Working method

Only developers write or modify runtime code and tests. The architect coordinates interfaces; physics and mathematics own meanings and operators; experimental review fixes independent expectations; documentation maintains definitions and evidence status. These roles do not imply continuously running agents. (The roles as they run since 2026-09-21 are in skills/workflow.md, "How the team works now", record 309 of LOG_2026-09-20.)

# 8. Documentation integrity check

The central specification owns adopted model decisions, the defined Detector and Node/Link acceptance, with open items identified explicitly. This document summarizes that owner rather than maintaining competing detailed laws. Review ordinary locality without exception, Detector-only sampling at marked Nodes, six-output timing and exact ownership. Distinguish unresolved numerical choices, engineering gaps and unproved emergence from already adopted principles. A candidate, unsupported profile or historical result must never silently override an adopted definition. (Since 2026-09-17 this file owns the adopted decisions, section 5.4; the central specification is the historical source up to the 2026-09-16 revision.)

# 9. Assistant working instruction

Do not suggest a next step or follow-up action unless Alon explicitly asks for it.

## Section 1 as it stood: the summary paragraph and the central specification

This English-language Highlights document summarizes the central model specification; it is not a competing source of physical laws. Section 3 restates the adopted principles at summary level. The central specification owns their full definitions, exceptions and acceptance criteria. Latest explicit user decisions supersede older prose. Adopted requirements, proposed numerical profiles, implemented mechanisms and tested results must remain distinct. An implementation gap does not reopen an adopted decision, and documentation must not invent a missing physical law. (Since 2026-09-17 this file is the authoritative Highlights text, the head of this document, and section 5.4 holds the law in force and the model owner's decisions; the central specification is the historical source up to the 2026-09-16 revision.)

[Central model specification: Universe24 — Unified Node Theory: a unifying schema for rays, fields and interactions.](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jPBMb-1BoCH8Qo6y5E-j0H0ANWzbHmkO9l-9t2pxSOQ/edit)

## Section 2 as it stood (2026-09-17)

The whole model, as decided on 2026-09-17, is four definitions and one principle; section 3 states each in full.

1. **Event and ray** (3.3, 3.20). A ray is a straight trajectory between two events and carries information. An event is where information splits, at a Node, by the declared coupling, into at most six rays. There is no third thing. (Under the law of events, 2026-09-19: read as section 5.4's law of events says, there being no ray, thing, shadow or bit, no draw and no return; what this describes is an event, in transit or measured, handled by the Node's one computation, and a Node keeps nothing.)
2. **Detector** (3.19, 5.4). A Node with a bit. On 1 the ray passes, and that pass is the only measurement. On 0 the Node returns the ray untouched, without reading it; the return cancels that ray's share of its event and carries it to the sibling lines. No register, nothing at a distance. (Under the law of events, 2026-09-19: read as section 5.4's law of events says, there being no ray, thing, shadow or bit, no draw and no return; what this describes is an event, in transit or measured, handled by the Node's one computation, and a Node keeps nothing.)
3. **Phase** (3.3). Every ray is a wave ray. Its phase advances at the rest rate of its family, which is its mass; light's rate is zero and it carries its emitter's clock. Interference is steering of content by phase difference, the Born rule as a declared table. Superseded on 2026-09-19 by the Beam Law (marked 2026-09-22): a row's phase is stamped by the emitter at birth and turned by its family's phase per Link at every Link crossed, a body's by its clock's pair K; the Born table is computed from N (5.4, point 17).
4. **Field** (3.5, 3.28). A ray's field is its own information spreading in ray form in all directions. It makes an event only where it meets something it changes: delay, bending, a changed trajectory, and the field ray returning with the opposite momentum. The computation field, which is gravity, obeys the same rule. (Under the law of events, 2026-09-19: read as section 5.4's law of events says, there being no ray, thing, shadow or bit, no draw and no return; what this describes is an event, in transit or measured, handled by the Node's one computation, and a Node keeps nothing.)

The principle (3.15): every declared invariant is exact, in bounded integers, at every event, because only then can an event be rebuilt from its parts when they return. (Under the law of events, 2026-09-19: read as section 5.4's law of events says, there being no ray, thing, shadow or bit, no draw and no return; what this describes is an event, in transit or measured, handled by the Node's one computation, and a Node keeps nothing.)

Since 2026-09-18 (the law of the bit, section 5.4) the four definitions read with one bit: every ray is a thing (1) or a shadow (0); a mark draws nothing, what arrives was decided at birth (point 14); the Born table is computed from N (point 17); a thing's clock is its content / K (point 19); the field is the thing's shadow set, given with the board, spreading by the Node's mixing (point 24), and its return after a push is a field, not a walk (point 3); nothing is delayed, every ray moves one Link per interval (point 21). Superseded on 2026-09-18 (the evening) by the law of the shadow, section 5.4: there is no bit; every ray is a shadow that spreads from an event by the Node's mixing, an event is a whole quantum at held content, absorbed, held or released again by the family's table, a click is such an absorption, nothing walks a path of its own and nothing returns; the Born table from N, the phase at content / K for every ray and one Link per interval stand. (Under the law of events, 2026-09-19: the definitions are one, the event; nothing splits below a whole, nothing waits at a Node, nothing returns, and an event in transit does not turn; section 5.4.)

Think of Universe24 as a kind of multidimensional Snake game with obstacles and interactions. Multiple rays move through the same 3D Node network across compatible property and field channels. They may cross without responding, respond weakly, or interact very strongly according to their selected coupling; crossing or co-location alone is not a collision. Here, weak and strong describe response strength, not automatically the fundamental weak and strong forces. Multidimensional includes independent state channels, not extra spatial dimensions. Obstacles are an analogy for declared interactions, not invented opaque walls or a capacity fix. Ordinary evolution is deterministic; only an actual Detector generates a draw (no draw since 2026-09-18, section 5.4, point 14). The central specification remains the precise definition. (Under the law of events, 2026-09-19: read as section 5.4's law of events says, there being no ray, thing, shadow or bit, no draw and no return; what this describes is an event, in transit or measured, handled by the Node's one computation, and a Node keeps nothing.)

## Sections 5.1 to 5.3 as they stood

### 5.1 Node state and ray form, before 2026-09-22

**State.** The state that moves is the ray (family properties, phase, heading, the number of steps it has made since its event, the information of its last event and, if that was a Detector event, its bit); a Node holds nothing but the rays resident this interval and, under a declared binding coupling, a bounded bound group. Since 2026-09-18 (section 5.4, definitions and points 22, 25): a ray carries an amount, a phase, a heading and a bit, a thing its momentum too; a shadow carries no step count (point 3); a Node is its six Ports, two lanes each, one real slot and one shadow slot per owner on every lane, with the parked shadows of point 22, and holds nothing else. Superseded on 2026-09-18 (the evening) by the law of the shadow, section 5.4: there is no bit and no real slot; every ray is a shadow, and a Node holds its six Ports, the parked shadows and, where it is matter, held content, which moves by its momentum (reading (v) there; the orchestrator's reading). (Under the law of events, 2026-09-19: read as section 5.4's law of events says, there being no ray, thing, shadow or bit, no draw and no return; what this describes is an event, in transit or measured, handled by the Node's one computation, and a Node keeps nothing.)

**Meetings.** At a meeting of rays the declared coupling between their families decides no interaction, a deterministic interaction with exact invariants and at most six events out, or a Detector interaction. There is no occupied channel and no capacity rule: rays cross, meet or bind by their declared couplings, and nothing is pushed back or made to wait for room. The occupied-channel displacement rule of the 2026-09-16 revision was deleted on 2026-09-17. Superseded for real rays on a lane on 2026-09-18 by point 25 of section 5.4 (model owner): a lane carries one real ray per interval, a thing steps into a lane only if the lane is free and otherwise keeps its heading and steps at the next Node, and two real rays of one family given one lane are one; nothing queues and nothing waits for room, the lane being a condition on the step and not a tie-break. Superseded on 2026-09-18 (the evening) by the law of the shadow, section 5.4: there is no real ray on a lane; a shadow that reaches held content is absorbed by the family's table, shadows of one number mix (point 24), and one real per lane and the merging of two reals are to be restated by round 8. (Under the law of events, 2026-09-19: read as section 5.4's law of events says, there being no ray, thing, shadow or bit, no draw and no return; what this describes is an event, in transit or measured, handled by the Node's one computation, and a Node keeps nothing.)

**Layers.** Event spacetime has layers: two events can happen at the same Node in the same interval in layers that do not communicate, because rays whose families have no declared coupling never meet; they cross as if the other were not there. A layer is a set of families that couple; a meeting exists only inside a layer.

### 5.2 Generic operations at a Node, before 2026-09-22

Arrived input, one bounded local update per tick, a local proposal and atomic commit. Physical execution is at the Node; the separate generic operations package is code organization, not another physical place. Immutable family and coupling definitions own physical transformations and conserved readouts. The engine schedules, transports and validates, while NodeState contains bounded data and ownership, not physical formulas.

**The Node's law in five steps (model owner, 2026-09-17).** A Node knows nothing about electrons or stars; it is a switchboard with six Ports, six output clocks and a table to read. Each interval: (1) receive what arrived on the six Ports, with what is resident (a bound group); (2) apply its mark, if any: a Detector draws once per arrival, 0 returned and 1 continued; an external body absorbs into its sink and radiates by its amount; (3) meet by table, layer by layer: families with no declared coupling cross as if alone, families with one produce the outputs the table says, with exact invariants and the remainder placed by section 3.17; (4) stamp every output as a new event ray, with its event's Ports, shares and steps 0; (5) depart, each ray through its Port when that face's clock is ready. The two marks, the Detector and the external body, are the whole apparatus of a world: they are the only places where the board does something the tables do not say, and both are declarations in the initial file, never physics. Since 2026-09-18 (section 5.4): a Node has no output clocks and no departure waits for one (point 21), the one wait being the tick of point 23; a mark draws nothing, it absorbs a thing and returns a shadow (points 6, 14); a shadow meeting a thing is a push and a return (point 3), the shadows of one owner are mixed among the six Ports (point 24), and the tables of step (3) stand for a thing meeting a thing. Superseded on 2026-09-18 (the evening) by the law of the shadow, section 5.4: no thing meets a thing and nothing is returned; each interval the Node mixes the shadows that arrived (point 24), and where it holds content it absorbs the whole quanta by the family's table, holds or releases again, and releases in proportion to its content, the step of held content being a release toward the neighbour and an absorption there (readings (i) and (v) there). (Under the law of events, 2026-09-19: read as section 5.4's law of events says, there being no ray, thing, shadow or bit, no draw and no return; what this describes is an event, in transit or measured, handled by the Node's one computation, and a Node keeps nothing.)

### 5.3 Couplings, fields and timing, before 2026-09-22

Propagation, funded emission, remainders, six independent output clocks, no input delay and fixed neighboring Link transit H. Mass representation, rest phase and computation delay are distinct. A free ray never meets its own field because the field is faster and leaves ahead of it or away from it (section 3.5); newly output-delayed moving emitters remain unsupported until their composition is defined and tested. The strong-interaction long-residence and computation-field-emission idea is a research hypothesis, not proof of nuclear binding; weak conversion channels need their own explicit operators. Both, and polarization, are catalog entries on the same engine (section 3.26), scheduled after feature 10. The six output clocks and the computation delay are superseded on 2026-09-18 by section 5.4, points 21 and 23: every ray moves one Link per interval, and the one wait is the tick a thing pays per whole quantum it reads. Superseded again on 2026-09-18 (the evening) by the law of the shadow, section 5.4: the one wait reads the size and is paid by every quantum, held or in flight (reading (iii) there); the emission is held content's, every interval in proportion to its content, and whether its gravity and electricity are free and its light paid is what round 8 must show. (Under the law of events, 2026-09-19: read as section 5.4's law of events says, there being no ray, thing, shadow or bit, no draw and no return; what this describes is an event, in transit or measured, handled by the Node's one computation, and a Node keeps nothing.)
